requirements.evidence: Migrations match the schema: `unique('entities_slug_unique')`, generated `owner_seq` `storedAs("CASE WHEN role = 'owner' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END")` and the unique index `entity_memberships_one_owner` (create_entity_memberships_table.php:19,23). The policies match the spec (EntityPolicy.php, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:28-38: owner never deletable, self-removal allowed). Pick route returns 403 before touching the session, writes the audit log and redirects (routes/web.php:54-71). Members: `exists:users,email`, duplicate is an error on `email`, role whitelist via `UserRole::manageable()`, owner/last manager gives 403 (Members.php:37-115). Settings: `#[Locked] public Entity $entity`, slug unique except itself, delete clears the session, transfer checks admin-of-this-entity/not-self/owner-vanished and runs in `DB::transaction` (Settings.php:41-115). Dashboard shows the settings link only when `$isOwner`. Lang keys exist in both locales. Gaps: `Log::channel('audit')?->` relies on an `audit` channel that is not shown in the diff, and the contract's untyped `$name`/`$slug`/`$targetMembershipId` are fine, but nothing ships to show the behaviour works.

conventions.evidence: No tests at all, which breaks the 'no production code without a test' rule. Domain writes (add/assign/remove member, save/delete/transfer entity, pick) happen inline in Livewire components and a route closure instead of `app/Actions/*` (Members.php:59-63, Settings.php:52-54, 106-112). Livewire uses inline `$this->validate([...])` arrays instead of the project's `#[Validate]` attributes (Members.php:37, Settings.php:47). CHANGELOG.md is not updated. Good: policies are registered and used, `$fillable` is set, Bulma and `x-form-field`/`x-button` components are reused, and docs/database-schema.md is updated.

security.evidence: Every public action re-resolves the entity and authorizes server-side (`$this->authorize('update', $entity)`, `authorize('assignRole', $membership)`, `authorize('delete', $membership)`, `authorize('manageSettings', $entity)`). Action IDs are scoped to the entity (`EntityMembership::where('entity_id', $entity->id)->findOrFail($membershipId)`). The entity property is `#[Locked]`, all output uses `{{ }}`, and `$fillable` is explicit. Minor gaps: `$targetMembershipId`, `$name` and `$slug` are untyped public properties, and `targetMembershipId` is never validated (it is only used in a scoped where, so the impact is limited). Sensitive actions such as delete and transfer are not rate-limited and have no confirmation.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files: no Pest feature tests for the policies, the pick route, the Livewire actions, unauthorized calls or tamper attempts. The conventions make these mandatory.

simplicity.evidence: The code is mostly direct. Some redundancy: Members re-fetches `Entity::findOrFail($this->entity->id)` in every method and in render even though the model is locked. The `if ($user === null)` branch after the `exists:users,email` rule is unreachable (Members.php:43-47). In removeMember the owner check happens both inline (Members.php:99) and in the policy, and `$isManager` checks for Owner, which can never be true there. The `Gate::policy` registrations may duplicate Laravel's automatic discovery.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and the methods are short. The `Gate::policy` lines were inserted between the existing layouts comment and the `Blade::anonymousComponentNamespace` call the comment describes (AppServiceProvider.php:40-45). The docs call the owner constraint a 'partial unique index' although it is a generated-column unique index. Business logic for pick lives in a route closure in routes/web.php.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task, and out-of-scope items (onboarding, switcher, middleware, navbar) are not built. The docs edit also drops `locale_default` from the entities ER diagram, which is a schema-proposal change the task did not ask for.

issues.explanation: No tests ship with the change, so policies, the pick route and every Livewire action lack happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call and tamper tests, which the project's TDD and Livewire policy make mandatory.
Domain writes (membership create/update/delete, entity save/delete, ownership transfer) are done inline in components instead of one `app/Actions/*` class per use case.
Validation uses inline rule arrays instead of the project's `#[Validate]` attribute pattern on public properties.
`$name`, `$slug` and `$targetMembershipId` are untyped, client-writable properties, and `targetMembershipId` is never validated (it is only used in an entity-scoped query, so the impact is limited).
The docs-sync convention requires a CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased], and none was added.
`Log::channel('audit')?->` uses a nullsafe call that is pointless here, and the change does not show that an `audit` channel exists or that the log line is verified.
The null-user branch is unreachable after the `exists:users,email` rule, and the repeated `Entity::findOrFail($this->entity->id)` duplicates the locked model.
The policy registrations were inserted between the layouts comment and the Blade namespace line it documents, so the comment now sits above the wrong code.
The change removes `locale_default` from the proposed entities schema, which the task did not ask for.

review.summary: The change implements the entities and memberships schema (including the DB-enforced single owner), the policies, the pick route and the Dashboard/Members/Settings Livewire pages, with sound server-side authorization and entity-scoped lookups. However, it ships no tests at all, which violates the mandatory TDD and Livewire security-test conventions. It also skips the Actions pattern and `#[Validate]` attributes, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
